title: The AI Ledger
introduction: Reviewed through November 22 at 20:00 UTC. This update adds Claude Code enterprise and session changes, a Qwen-derived open-weight model, and a research note on perplexity. Late additions keep their original release dates. The November 21 snapshot is preserved unchanged. The Mythos access forecast is not resolved ahead of its 23:59 UTC deadline; the next-week controls forecast keeps its original criteria. No fresh rumor met the evidence threshold.

items.title: Added Nov 22: Claude Code 2.1.330 improves enterprise sign-in and session recovery
items.summary: The release adds sign-in for organizations managed in Anthropic’s Enterprise Admin Console; Claude Code applies organization settings and uses its provider or gateway. It also lets self-hosted runners start work in a repository subdirectory.
items.whyItMatters: Regression-test long-session compaction and resume, concurrent settings saves, and worktree ownership. Anthropic reports fixes for freezes after compaction, invalid timestamps on resume, and worktree deletion while another session is using it.
items.historicalContext: GitHub published this version November 20 at 22:32 UTC. This is a harness update, not a Claude model launch. A GitHub release does not establish that every updater channel has promoted the version.
items.confidenceReason: Primary publisher documentation supports the described release or proposal. Reported results have not been independently reproduced here.

items.title: Added Nov 22: RadixArk publishes DaisyRose-27B weights
items.summary: RadixArk used reinforcement learning to adapt Qwen3.8-27B for long-horizon agent tasks. Its model card lists Apache-2.0 weights in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4, retaining the base tokenizer, image input and 256K context.
items.whyItMatters: On Terminal-Bench 4.1, RadixArk reports 12.0% pass@1 versus 5.6% for the base model. That is a publisher-reported comparison, not an independent result or a guarantee for a different harness.
items.historicalContext: The publisher’s announcement is dated November 18. A later inference-provider listing does not make this a new November 22 model launch.

items.title: Research note: OpenAI proposes shared perplexity tracking
items.summary: OpenAI published historical measurements of next-token prediction on its held-out internal codebase and proposed exploring a shared cross-lab measure for pretraining progress and safety milestones.
items.whyItMatters: Treat it as a research proposal, not a coding-agent leaderboard. The article discusses dataset choice and the fact that improvements from reasoning after pretraining are not captured by this metric.
items.historicalContext: Published November 22. It does not announce a new model, availability, pricing, or an adopted industry standard.

items.title: Inkling 2 Mini ships open weights for local inference
items.summary: Thinking Machines released Apache-2.0 weights for a model that accepts text and images and generates text. The model card gives 26.4B total and 3.4B active parameters, or 5.4B effective active per token when repeated layer passes count.
items.whyItMatters: The native checkpoint weighs about 20 GB, not the total runtime memory. The lab lists Apple silicon with at least 32 GB and DGX Spark as supported hardware, and recommends at least 32 GB VRAM for other GPU setups. Treat the model’s 1M-token maximum as a capability ceiling, not a guarantee on minimum hardware.
items.historicalContext: Released November 20 and added in the November 21 review. Ollama’s library confirms a local package; its headline active count uses the repeated computation figure, not a different model.
